title: Sir Walter Raleigh, Petavius, Gautruche Poetical Cognates, Parian Chronicle, Classical Rome & Periplus

nodes.name: Raleigh & Methodius's 3 Post-Flood Leaders: Nimrod (Ham), Joktan (Shem) & Suphene (Japheth)
nodes.era: Post-Flood Dispersion (Raleigh 1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VII p. 69; Petavius 1659)
nodes.role: Tripartite Dispersion Commanders of Ham, Shem & Japheth
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VII p. 69)
nodes.notes: Sir Walter Raleigh (citing Methodius of Tyre) records the three post-Flood commanders who led the peoples after Babel: Nimrod over Ham's line, Joktan over Shem's line, and Suphene over Japheth's line — framed within Petavius's universal chronology from Creation.

nodes.name: Raleigh's Shemite Plantation of the East Indies: Joktan, Havilah & Ophir
nodes.era: Eastward Dispersion (Raleigh 1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Map)
nodes.role: Biblical Shemite Pioneers of India & the East Indies
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Engraved Noahic Map)
nodes.notes: Raleigh argues at length in Book I Ch. VIII (and marks on his engraved dispersion map) that Joktan's descendants Havilah and Ophir planted the regions stretching across Persia and India / the East Indies.

nodes.name: Raleigh's Cushite Arabia the Happy: Seba, Sabtah & Raamah (Sabe Regia & Aden)
nodes.era: Post-Flood Arabia (Raleigh 1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Map)
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VIII & Map)
nodes.notes: Raleigh maps Cush's sons Seba, Sabtah, and Raamah (Rhegma) directly along the coasts and cities of Arabia the Happy (Arabia Felix), including Sabe Regia and Aden.

nodes.name: Cato's Scythia Saga (Raleigh p. 69): Post-Flood Scythians → Galli (Gauls) & Italian Umbri
nodes.role: Classical Witness to mankind's Post-Flood Restoration via Scythia & Italy
sources: Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Vol. 1 Book I Ch. VII p. 69, citing Cato)
nodes.notes: Raleigh quotes Cato (Fragments) that after mankind was restored following the Deluge, populations spread from Scythia Saga into the Galli (Gauls) and ancient Umbri of Italy.

nodes.name: Gautruche's Poetical History Cognates: Golden Age (Saturn/Janus = Noah), Silver Age (Jupiter = Ham), Brazen Age (Nimrod), Vulcan (= Tubal-Cain) & Apollo (= Jubal)
nodes.role: Systematic Identification of Greco-Roman Mythic Figures with Genesis Patriarchs
nodes.notes: Gautruche translates Greco-Roman mythology back into Biblical history: the Golden Age under Saturn/Janus corresponds to Noah (threefold division of the world), the Silver Age to Jupiter (Ham/Cham), the Brazen Age to Nimrod, Vulcan to metal-worker Tubal-Cain, and Apollo to musician Jubal.

nodes.name: The Parian Chronicle (264 BCE Marble) & Lucian: Epoch 1 Cecrops (1582 BCE) & Epoch 2 Deucalion's Flood (1529 BCE)
nodes.era: 264 BCE Greek Inscription (The Parian Chronicle 1788 pp. 1-5; Lucian De Dea Syria)
nodes.role: Epigraphic Greek Chronicle & Syrian Flood Witness
sources: The Parian Chronicle or Chronicle of the Arundelian Marbles (1788 pp. 1-5)
nodes.notes: Inscribed in marble on Paros in 264 BCE, the Parian Chronicle anchors Greek chronology at Epoch 1 (Cecrops, first king of Athens, 1582 BCE) and Epoch 2 (Deucalion escaping the Great Flood to Athens from Parnassus, 1529 BCE), paired with Lucian's De Dea Syria preserving the Near Eastern Deluge tradition under Deucalion's name.

nodes.name: Classical Persian-Greek Bridge (Xenophon, Curtius Rufus & Plutarch): Artaxerxes II Mnemon, Cyrus the Younger (401 BCE) & Darius III
nodes.role: Late Achaemenid Emperors Leading to Alexander the Great
sources: Quintus Curtius Rufus History of Alexander
nodes.notes: Documented across Xenophon's Anabasis (Cyrus the Younger vs. his brother Artaxerxes II at Cunaxa, 401 BCE), Plutarch, and Curtius Rufus down to Darius III and Alexander the Great.

nodes.name: Classical Roman Imperial Spine (Livy, Tacitus, Echard 5 Vols., Ammianus & Mexía): Vespasian & Titus (70 CE) → Trajan → Marcus Aurelius → Diocletian → Romulus Augustulus (476 CE)
nodes.era: 69–476 CE (Echard Vols. 2-4; Tacitus; Ammianus Marcellinus; Mexía)
nodes.role: Flavians, Five Good Emperors, Tetrarchy & Western Roman Finale
nodes.notes: Synthesizes the Roman imperial succession across Echard's 5-volume Roman History, Tacitus, Ammianus Marcellinus, Florus, Aurelius Victor, and Mexía from Vespasian & Titus through Trajan, Marcus Aurelius, Diocletian, and Romulus Augustulus (476 CE) to Charlemagne (Echard Vol. 5).

nodes.name: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (Vincent 1800): King Zoscales of Aksum, Saba/Sheba, Ophir & Red Sea–India Corridor
nodes.era: 1st c. CE (William Vincent Periplus of the Erythrean Sea, 1800)
nodes.role: Classical Greco-Egyptian Maritime Bridge Linking Aksum, Sheba, Arabia & India
sources: William Vincent The Periplus of the Erythrean Sea (1800)
nodes.notes: Vincent's scholarly commentary identifies King Zoscales of Aksum (Adulis, 1st c. CE), maps classical Saba/Mariaba to Biblical Sheba, examines the Ophir trade corridor, and documents direct monsoon voyages linking Ethiopia and Arabia to western India.
